Krichene and Rendle (KDD 2020) show that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model orderings relative to full-catalog metrics, even in expectation; smaller candidate samples also make ranking metrics behave increasingly like AUC. Thus HR@10 against 99 negatives measures performance under that candidate protocol and does not establish full-catalog HR@10 superiority. Corrections can reduce estimation error, but cannot be substituted into this pinned benchmark. [On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

Recommended uncertainty analysis: compare models on identical validation users and candidate sets; bootstrap users as paired observations within each category, recomputing the equally weighted four-category mean difference for every replicate. Report the difference and interval alongside category results. This adapts paired bootstrap evaluation to the benchmark; its uncertainty is conditional on the fixed candidate samples and trained models, excluding negative-sampling and training-seed variation. [Koehn, 2004](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/)

Repeated checkpoint and hyperparameter selection can overfit validation feedback, making the winning validation score optimistic. Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals computed after adaptive selection do not remove this selection bias. Practical implication: predefine the selection rule, record all trials, treat small validation gains cautiously, and reserve the untouched host test evaluation for the final selected model. Keep the mandated splits and evaluator unchanged; full-catalog simulator recommendations address a different evaluation setting. [Cawley and Talbot, 2010](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [The reusable holdout](https://research.google/blog/the-reusable-holdout-preserving-validity-in-adaptive-data-analysis/)
